entries.heading: Senior Data Engineer
bullets: Product pins obscured the 360° panorama during admin inspection; added a self-contained toggle inside the shared krpano viewer component, gating the overlay behind a module-level stable empty array to avoid re-render churn in its animation-frame effect — one change covered all three viewer usages.

Operators had no way to tag which room a viewpoint belonged to; regenerated the typed API client from swagger and added a searchable, clearable AntD Select to the point-detail modal wired to a new PATCH with optimistic update, rollback on error and query-key invalidation — room assignment and unassignment work for both point types with no full-list refetch

Re-architected a microservice into two purpose-built services: an internal admin API with normalized tables for data integrity, and a public client-facing API with denormalized tables collapsed into just 3 endpoints — eliminating network round trips entirely and enabling front-end caching for significantly faster reads

Built and owned the full end-to-end panorama generation pipeline: from 2D point placement on a canvas in the React admin panel, through task creation in the panorama microservice, to an Unreal Engine polling client that generates cube maps, uploads them back to the microservice, and renders them on interactive floor plans via krpano

A three-hop redirect chain broke WebGL texture loads on CORS and served wrong MIME types; designed a Go read service collapsing it to a single streamed response — one tenant-scoped JOIN for resolution, DB-driven Content-Type, ACAO, and Range/ETag/304 via http.ServeContent — fixing both defects at serve time for already-broken objects, with Docker Compose wiring.

Concurrent producers were stamping read-model snapshot versions independently of when content was read, so an older read could win the last-writer-wins gate and freeze stale data; bound version allocation to content by running sequence allocation and the full slice build inside one PostgreSQL RepeatableRead transaction — correctness restored under multi-producer load with the change contained to a single dispatcher class.
Diagnosed and resolved a subtle React <StrictMode> double-invocation bug that was silently breaking krpano pin rendering

An admin-side background service reconciled projections by reading the public service's schema directly, breaking the events-only service boundary; replaced it with a lean Kafka census contract plus a read-side prune consumer and blind write-side re-emit, deleting the reconciliation service and its cross-project references — neither service references the other's schema any more.

A single poison row in the projection invalidation queue re-drained forever and blocked all downstream work; added per-row exception isolation with bounded retry/dead-lettering plus a unique index and ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING migration to coalesce duplicate signals — the queue now drains past failures instead of stalling.

Unreal's visibility test leaked neighbouring-room products into apartment tours; after adjudicating that the fix belonged at serve time rather than bake time, added a subtractive room predicate to the public tour projector with an explicit fallback for unassigned hotspots — a room reassignment now takes effect on the next request with zero re-bake, no schema, query or endpoint change

Apartment cards shipped with no thumbnail because nothing ever populated the field; added a focused EF Core repository read (deterministic ordering, scalar-column filter for query translation) plus a projector fallback with per-cycle caching, keeping any manual value winning — thumbnails appear automatically within one 60-second sync cycle, with no migration and no backfill

Every uploaded object was stored as application/octet-stream despite the DB recording the real type; set the content type from the recorded value at S3 write — correct MIME for all future uploads across every consumer

entries.heading: Lead Data Engineer
bullets: Optimized Windows version by refactoring UI with a view pattern and implementing event-driven logic, reducing FPS drop by 97% (from 60 to 2 FPS).

Developed a native Unreal host enabling .NET integration to leverage a free CAD library, implemented CAD-to-UE data conversion, and created a UStructSynchronizer to sync Unreal USTRUCTs with C# counterparts.

entries.heading: Staff Data Engineer
bullets: Architected data structures and flows in Unreal Engine to represent 3D apartment objects, and built a custom packaging system that resolved asset dependencies via the Content Browser, categorized them automatically, and deployed the resulting .pak files to Amazon S3

Integrated REST API-based user authentication and a custom analytics tracking system recording dwell time per apartment and per-object interaction events, aggregating the data into structured reports dispatched to a backend endpoint
Developed custom Unreal Engine commandlets in C# to automate and streamline build and packaging pipelines, reducing manual overhead in the deployment workflow
Developed high-performance widgets with custom styling using the Slate Framework
Developed utility modules reducing boilerplate in threaded operations, including Blueprint-friendly async wrappers, Rust-style result handling, and enhanced automation testing
Developed UI system from scratch using Presenter pattern for separation of concerns. Created customizable, reusable components matching Figma designs with system-wide configuration support
Developed cross-platform marketplace widget with platform-specific layouts and reusable components (filters, search, list selectors)

Led a team of four developers, assigning tasks, managing disputes, and maintaining project coordination through an internal task tracker. Conducted biweekly progress meetings and architectural discussions. Wrote and maintained documentation for company guidelines and production pipelines

The project suffered from poor performance and FPS drops due to frequent garbage collection during level loading. I refactored the system to use asynchronous loading and implemented object pooling to pre-create and reuse objects. This significantly increased performance

entries.heading: Senior Backend Engineer
bullets: Integrated a REST API to fetch product data with multi-variant structures, translating JSON responses into a dynamic UI that updated available options in real time based on variant availability
Engineered a cascading variant filtration system where each selection progressively narrowed subsequent options, ensuring only valid variant combinations were surfaced to the user

Integrated two caching mechanisms: one memory-based and one file-based. The memory cache used a singleton to store generic data in memory, while the file-based cache handled byte-convertible assets such as dynamic meshes stored in the cloud. This integration dramatically improved performance, as no caching existed previously

Refactored furniture moving system by isolating movement logic into testable components, decoupling input handling, and applying dependency injection. This improved architecture enabled faster feature integration
Built grouped object system for moving object clusters with serialized selection state, streamlining apartment design with repeated elements

Led a team of four developers, assigning tasks based on their skills and providing support when needed. Implemented Agile and Scrum practices to create a customized task pipeline, improving communication between developers and managers
